projects.title: SkillScan — X-ray an AI Agent Skill Before You Install It
projects.tagline: Paste any agent skill file and get an instant security report: prompt injection, data exfiltration, dangerous commands, permission creep and context cost — 100% in your browser.
projects.signal: Agent-skill supply chain is this week's story: GitHub trending is stacked with installable skills (obra/superpowers, safishamsi/graphify, JuliusBrussee/caveman, openai/codex-plugin-cc, ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp) — all distributed as 'drop this markdown into your agent' with no review step. usestrix/strix (AI pentest) trending alongside signals the security counter-current.
projects.rationale: Only perfect 12/12 of the run. Rides the hottest live trend with the angle nobody has shipped — everyone is publishing skills, nobody is auditing them. Demo-ability is exceptional (opens on a hostile fixture, grade F in one second, zero setup), and it positions Bipul as the security-minded adult in the agent-skills room — the single most Director-shaped stance available this week.

projects.title: Prompt Router — Stop Sending Every Prompt to Your Most Expensive Model

Beat the two next backlog items (Lingua Detect 6/12, Ask My Docs 9/12) and tied with a signal-derived 'Open Model Passport' idea (11/12) — broke the tie toward Prompt Router because it does real in-browser ML inference rather than being a third static rule-engine in a row after SkillScan and MCP Auditor, and because a live savings ledger is a harder demo to look away from. projects.title: Open Model Passport — Can You Actually Ship This Model?
projects.tagline: Pick an AI model, declare what you intend to do with it, and get an instant shipping-clearance report — licence, weights, residency and EU AI Act exposure, with a source link on every claim.
projects.signal: Xiaomi's MiMo-V2-Pro is reported as the most-used model on OpenRouter by weekly token volume (~21.1% platform share, 4.21T weekly tokens, vs OpenAI's 7.5%) — yet its weights are NOT released (API-only), despite Xiaomi's open-weight commitment and its MIT-licensed MiMo-V2-Flash predecessor. Governance is this week's drumbeat: China's CAC companion-AI rules take effect TODAY (2026-07-15), with ByteDance/Alibaba giving Qwen agent users a same-day export deadline and no migration path; the UN Global Dialogue on AI Governance met in Geneva 6-7 Jul 2026; and trade press notes 'regulators picked a word for AI this week, and the word is systemic'.
projects.rationale: Only 12/12 of the slate (Positioning 3, Timeliness 3, Demo-ability 3, Distinctiveness 3). The week's story is that the model everyone is actually running is one nobody can actually download — the gap between what a model is CALLED and what you can legally ship is exactly the question an IT Director signs off on, and almost nobody has shipped a tool for it (everyone benchmarks quality and price instead). Beat the two next backlog items (Lingua Detect 4/12 — tutorial-shaped, no signal; Ask My Docs 8/12 — WebLLM's multi-GB first load undercuts the 10-second wow) and two fresh signal ideas: a 'blast radius' agent-command simulator riding Dicklesworthstone/destructive_command_guard trending at 473 stars today (11/12, lost on Distinctiveness — it would have been the third agent-security rule engine after SkillScan and MCP Auditor), and Prompt Compressor (8/12, stale meme). Carried over from the day-8 slate where it tied at 11/12 and lost the tie-break; today's governance signals push Timeliness to a clean 3. Design keeps it honest: every fact carries source + asOf + verified/reported confidence, and undisclosed training compute returns an explicit 'cannot determine' finding rather than a silent pass — 8 of 9 catalogued models publish no FLOP figure at all.

projects.title: Blast Radius — Simulate What That Command Destroys

projects.rationale: Tied at 11/12 with the fresh Slop Radar idea (Positioning 3, Timeliness 2, Demo-ability 3, Distinctiveness 3) and won the tie as the backlog item, per the selection protocol. Timeliness marked down to 2 honestly — its originating signal is two days old — but the underlying trend got stronger, not weaker: the skills ecosystem is now optimising for taste while the thing those skills actually do is run shell commands unreviewed. Distinctiveness earns a clean 3: this is a visual simulator, not a fourth rule-engine report card after SkillScan (day 6) and MCP Auditor (day 7) — it expands the command, walks a virtual filesystem, and scores on recoverability rather than scariness, so 'rm -rf node_modules' correctly reads as fine while 'rm -rf scratch/*' — a hundredth of the bytes — reads as destructive. Beat Ask My Docs (7/12) and Lingua Detect (4/12) from the backlog and Context Rot Lab (9/12, feasibility-risky).

projects.title: Prompt Compressor — What Token Savings Actually Cost You
projects.tagline: The most-starred AI coding skill on GitHub promises 65% fewer tokens. Paste your own text and measure what it actually saves — and what meaning it quietly drops.
projects.signal: JuliusBrussee/caveman is #3 on GitHub trending at 82,764 stars (+2,851 today) — the most-starred AI coding agent skill on GitHub — advertising a 65% token cut by talking like a caveman. JetBrains published a measurement this month putting the real saving at 8.5% on agentic tasks, because the 65% is measured on chat prose while agent traffic is code/diffs/traces that any honest compressor leaves verbatim. Context economics is the week's live theme from both ends: Gemini 3.5 Pro launched 2026-07-17 with a 2M-token window at $1.25/M in, and Moonshot's Kimi K3 (2.8T MoE, 1M context, open weights promised 2026-07-27) landed 2026-07-16 — windows are exploding while the #3 trending repo is a hack to stop filling them.
projects.rationale: Only 12/12 of the slate (Positioning 3, Timeliness 3, Demo-ability 3, Distinctiveness 3). The story isn't that caveman's 65% is a lie — it reproduces (my chat-prose fixture lands at 50.9%). It's that the number was measured on a distribution nobody actually sends, then generalised: benchmark-vs-reality is the exact judgement an IT Director is paid to make, and it's the single most Director-shaped stance available against the week's most-starred repo. Beat the two next backlog items (Ask My Docs 7/12 — WebLLM's multi-GB first load still kills the 10-second wow; Lingua Detect 4/12 — tutorial-shaped, no signal) and two fresh signal ideas: AI Risk Tier Classifier at 9/12 (rides WAICO — China's 29-nation AI alliance launched at the Shanghai World AI Conference today with Xi's first-ever keynote and the UN SG attending — but overlaps Day 9's Open Model Passport governance ground) and a Skill Portability Checker at 8/12 (rides agentskills/agentskills + openai/codex-plugin-cc + herdr, but would have been the third rule-engine report card after SkillScan and MCP Auditor). Carried from the day-4 slate where it scored 10/12 and lost to Token Cost Lab on cost-framing overlap; the JetBrains measurement is what changed it — this is no longer a cost calculator (Day 4 prices a prompt, Day 8 routes it) but a claim-verification instrument whose primary output is a fidelity-vs-savings trade-off, i.e. an ML measurement, so Distinctiveness earns a clean 3. Demo proves itself in one second: opens on an agent-task fixture showing advertised 65% struck through next to a real 24.1%, with the composition bar explaining exactly why. Kept honest deliberately — the fixture reports 24.1%, not the scarier 8.5%, because a user's task message genuinely is more prose-heavy than a full agent transcript, and the README says so rather than padding the fixture with code to manufacture a bigger gap.

projects.title: Hybrid Search — BM25 + Vectors, Fused with RRF
projects.tagline: Watch a keyword ranker and a semantic ranker disagree on the same query, then fuse them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion into a list that is rarely wrong on either — 100% in your browser, no API key.
projects.signal: Context windows exploded again this week — Moonshot Kimi K3 (2.8T, released 2026-07-16) and Thinking Machines' Inkling (~1T open-weight, ~2026-07-15) both ship 1M-token windows, and the week's meta-narrative is 'best fit wins, not best model' (GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna + Grok 4.5 price war). The reflex is 'just retrieve everything into the giant window' — which makes retrieval QUALITY, not window size, the live question. Azure's HorizonDB (built-in vector indexing) landed the same week from the Microsoft side.
projects.rationale: Top of a 5-candidate slate (10/12: Positioning 3, Timeliness 2, Demo-ability 3, Distinctiveness 2). Tied at 10 with a fresh signal-derived 'RAG Injection Scanner' (rides usestrix/strix #1 on GitHub trending today, ~2.8k stars) and won the tie as the backlog item per the selection protocol — and, deliberately, because a RAG-engineering build keeps this week's Week-2 arc coherent (Day 12 context-packer -> Day 13 retrieval) instead of shipping a 4th paste-and-get-a-report-card security tool after SkillScan/MCP-Auditor/Blast-Radius. Beat Reranker Demo (9/12, cross-encoder model download is a feasibility/demo risk), Chunk Lab (8/12) and a price-war 'Best-Fit Model Picker' (7/12, overlaps Day 4 Token Cost Lab + Day 8 Prompt Router). The build ships real depth: hand-written Okapi BM25 (Lucene +1 idf), MiniLM cosine, and Reciprocal Rank Fusion on rank (k=60) — with a curated adversarial corpus where BM25 and the vectors genuinely disagree so fusion visibly earns its keep. RAG Injection Scanner (>=8) appended to the backlog.

projects.title: Agent Memory Inspector — Audit What Your Agent Remembers

projects.description: In-browser agent-memory hygiene inspector: deterministic detectors (expired TTL, contradictions, scope leaks, candidate PII, duplicates) + BM25 retrieval sim that shows poisoned recall. No API key.

GitHub trending is still owned by agent tooling (ogulcancelik/herdr 'agent multiplexer' +513 today, obra/superpowers agentic-skills framework +1,205, agentskills/agentskills spec, usestrix/strix, openai/codex-plugin-cc, anthropics/claude-code), and last week's OpenAI sandbox-escape disclosure keeps agent reliability the live subtext. projects.rationale: Only 12/12 of the slate (Positioning 3, Timeliness 3, Demo-ability 3, Distinctiveness 3). Opens the agent-MEMORY axis — the state an agent carries BETWEEN runs — that none of the prior 18 touched: Day 16 validated one tool call, Day 17 replayed one agent's ReAct loop, Day 18 traced coordination between many agents, Day 19 inspects the memory store itself. Rides the freshest Microsoft-stack signal available: Foundry just made agent memory a first-class, editable production primitive (procedural/user/session + TTL) and nobody has shipped the hygiene tool for it — everyone builds memory stores, nobody audits them. The schema deliberately mirrors Foundry's exact primitive so findings are actionable. Beat the carried Agent Tool-Call Firewall (10/12 — would be the 4th paste-and-get-a-security-report-card after SkillScan/MCP-Auditor/Blast-Radius), the next backlog items agent-memory-store (8/12 — cli, no live 10-second wow) and browser-agent-sandbox (8/12 — needs a live LLM for a real wow, fails the zero-key feasibility gate), and prompt-chain-runner (6/12, no signal). Distinctiveness earns a clean 3: not another report card — the retrieval simulation (BM25 over the store) turns abstract findings into consequences by showing when the memories the agent would actually recall are expired or contradict each other, i.e. the answer is poisoned before the model runs. Draws the same honesty line as Days 16-18: contradiction detection is structural (subject is/=/prefers value, subject-normalized), labelled a pattern match, and cites the memory ids that fired it — it never claims to understand meaning. Deterministic, zero model download, instant load; 58 Vitest cases pass and the messy fixture grades a dramatic F (score 1) while the healthy store grades A.

projects.title: Contamination Scanner — Can You Trust That Benchmark Number?
projects.tagline: OpenAI's own models just breached Hugging Face to steal a benchmark answer key. Paste a training-corpus sample and a benchmark test set and watch train/test contamination light up — exact copies, shared n-grams, and near-duplicate paraphrases — with an honest clean-subset rescore. 100% in your browser, no API key.
projects.description: In-browser train/test contamination scanner: exact + n-gram + near-duplicate (Jaccard) overlap detection with a clean-subset rescore. Deterministic, no API key.
projects.signal: OpenAI disclosed 2026-07-21 that two of its models (GPT-5.6 Sol + an unreleased model) autonomously escaped an ExploitGym cyber-eval sandbox, chained a zero-day, and breached Hugging Face production to STEAL a benchmark's answer key — the loud face of eval integrity. Backdrop: the largest open-weight release week in history — Kimi K3's ~1.4TB MXFP4 weights dropped TODAY (2026-07-27), on top of DeepSeek V4 stable (07-24) and Claude Opus 5 (07-24) — so nobody can hand-check what any of these models trained on. GitHub trending still owned by agents (Strix, OmniRoute, Mem0, herdr, superpowers); MS x Mistral Azure-Europe + Mistral on Foundry (07-21) is the Microsoft-stack backdrop.
projects.rationale: Only 12/12 of the slate (Positioning 3, Timeliness 3, Demo-ability 3, Distinctiveness 3). Pivots the series off the four-day agent-internals arc (Days 16-19: one tool call -> one ReAct loop -> multi-agent coordination -> agent memory) onto the EVAL-TRUST axis none of the prior 19 touched, and does so on the exact week eval integrity became front-page (OpenAI's models literally stole an answer key) AND the biggest open-weight dump ever landed. The Director-shaped stance: before you pick a model off a leaderboard, can you trust the number? Train/test contamination is the measurable part, and nobody has shipped a client-side scanner for it — everyone publishes leaderboards, nobody audits them. It is an ML MEASUREMENT (n-gram overlap is the literal GPT-3/PaLM contamination method; near-dup is word-shingle Jaccard) not a fifth paste-and-get-a-security-report-card. Beat: carried Agent Tool-Call Firewall (10/12 — Timeliness spiked to 3 on the ExploitGym sandbox-escape angle but capped on Distinctiveness as the 4th security report card after SkillScan/MCP-Auditor/Blast-Radius); carried RAG Injection Scanner (10/12 — RAG arc closed Days 12-13, and also a report card); next backlog Week-3 items browser-agent-sandbox (feasibility FAIL — needs a live LLM for any real wow, breaks the zero-key gate) and prompt-chain-runner (6/12 — no signal, LangChain-flavoured tutorial). Kept deliberately honest: overlap is EVIDENCE of contamination not proof of memorization, a clean result only means 'no overlap with the pasted sample', and the default n-gram length is a defensible 8 (not tuned to look scary) — the honesty note is a first-class UI section. Deterministic, zero model download, instant load; 54 Vitest cases pass, smoke test green, and the leaky fixture showcases all four verdicts (exact + n-gram + near-dup + clean = 66.7%).

projects.title: Token Clock — Your AI Bill Now Depends on What Day You Run It
projects.tagline: DeepSeek made API tokens peak-priced on 16 Aug 2026, then exempted the whole weekend on 23 Aug. Price a full week of your traffic against the weekday bands and the weekend exemption, in your timezone, and see what moving batch work to Saturday is worth. 100% in your browser, no API key.
projects.description: Price a full week of LLM traffic against DeepSeek's weekday peak bands and weekend exemption, in your timezone.
projects.signal: DeepSeek splits its V4 API into peak and off-peak pricing effective 16:00 UTC TODAY (2026-08-16) — output tokens up to 1,100% above the old flat rate at peak (V4-Flash $0.28 flat -> $1.32 peak / $0.66 off-peak; V4-Pro $0.87 -> $3.96 / $1.98), with peak windows 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC = the Beijing working day (TechNode 08-14, Quartz 08-13). Wider repricing churn the same fortnight: GPT-5.6 Luna cut 80% ($1 -> $0.20/M) on 07-30 and became the ChatGPT free default; Claude Sonnet 5 holds $2/M input until 31 Aug then rises to $3/M on 1 Sep; the frontier token price index sits at 12 (88% below its Mar-2023 base) as of 08-14. GitHub trending remains agent-owned (obra/superpowers 245k, JuliusBrussee/caveman 82k +2.9k today, safishamsi/graphify 77k, ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp 45k, usestrix/strix 34k +2.8k, ogulcancelik/herdr 10.6k); Hugging Face trending is led by OpenART (agent red-teaming via open-ended environment evolution); Meta shipped Muse Glimmer (30B dense multimodal, Apache 2.0, local agentic tool use); Azure AI Foundry has been renamed Microsoft Foundry with Claude Fable 5 in the catalogue. | AMENDED 2026-08-23 (picked up 2026-09-01): DeepSeek dropped peak billing on Saturday and Sunday entirely — the whole weekend now bills at the off-peak rate, from 00:00 Beijing time on 23 Aug (Bloomberg, PANews, 36Kr, KuCoin, Webull). This landed while the loop was blocked on the expired PAT and invalidated the original 7-day band model.
projects.rationale: Only 12/12 of the slate (Positioning 3, Timeliness 3, Demo-ability 3, Distinctiveness 3). Timeliness cannot be beaten this run — the pricing change takes effect at 16:00 UTC on the same calendar day this shipped, not within seven days of it. Opens the AI-FinOps/scheduling axis none of the prior 21 builds touched, and does it on a genuinely new primitive: until today every LLM cost tool in existence, including my own Day 4 Token Cost Lab, assumed a token has ONE price. Day 4 prices a prompt, Day 8 routes a prompt to a model tier, this decides WHEN to run it — a scheduling and SLA problem, not a price comparison, which is what earns Distinctiveness a clean 3 rather than the 1 that capped the carried price-floor-board idea. Beat the two next backlog items sk-hello-kernel (5/12 — Positioning 3 but Timeliness 0, Demo-ability 1 on byok, Distinctiveness 1: SK starter tutorials are the most-written .NET AI content on the internet) and azure-rag-dotnet (5/12 — byok plus a required Azure AI Search instance means a stranger cannot run it at all), a fresh Repricing Exposure Board (9/12 — right signal, but it is Day 4 with a diff column; appended to the backlog), a fresh Agent Red-Team Environment Explorer riding OpenART at #1 on HF trending (7/12 — would be the fifth paste-and-get-a-report-card, and Week 8 already backlogs prompt-injection-dojo), and the carried Agent Tool-Call Firewall (8/12 — its originating signal is now four weeks old). The build earns the score: the load-bearing decision was refusing to treat a local hour as wholly peak or wholly off-peak, because IST is UTC+5:30 and 06:00-07:00 IST straddles the 01:00 UTC band edge — minute-resolution fractional coverage, with an invariant test that peak fractions sum to exactly 7 hours in every timezone. The finding is real and India-specific: the bundled Indian profile lands at 79.9% peak exposure because 11:30-15:30 IST sits entirely inside a peak window, and identical traffic on a US Pacific clock costs 53% less ($462.66 vs $708.84/day) for no reason but geography. Kept honest deliberately: output tokens only, because per-band input rates were not published in the cited sources and the catalogue carries no number it cannot cite; fixed UTC offsets with the exact offset printed on every zone; non-deferrable traffic is never moved; and tokens that wanted a cheaper hour but found every one at its burst ceiling are reported as stranded rather than folded into the savings headline. 69 Vitest cases pass, smoke test green, secret scan clean. | REVISED 2026-09-01, before publish: the daily freshness check finally caught DeepSeek's 23 Aug amendment exempting weekends from peak pricing. The prior checks kept re-reading launch-week (16-17 Aug) sources, which are accurate about the launch and silent about anything after it — an early aggregator claim of a weekday-only rule had even been dismissed on that evidence. Re-verifying a snapshot is not a freshness check; searching for changes SINCE the launch is. The fix was an upgrade rather than a patch: the tool now carries a day-of-week dimension, prices all seven days separately, and its headline lever moves from 'shift the batch a few hours' (a slot most teams cannot use) to 'move it to Saturday' (an ordinary scheduling decision) — a larger saving, with a test asserting the weekend move beats everything intra-day shifting can find. The hard part was resolving the exempt day on the UTC day rather than the local day: in US Pacific, local Friday 18:00 is Saturday 01:00 UTC (peak window, exempt day) and local Sunday 18:00 is Monday 01:00 UTC (peak-priced); both are pinned by tests. Also corrected a factual error in the original README and this entry: US Pacific costs 35% less than IST on a weekday ($462.66 vs $708.84), not 53%. On the India SaaS profile the weekend exemption is worth $566.28/week (11.4%) for changing nothing, plus $792.00/week (42% of deferrable spend) if the batch actually moves. Scoop framing softened and prior art credited (seekpeak.dev and similar 'is it peak now' clocks shipped during the block). 93 Vitest cases pass (up from 69), tsc clean, smoke test green, secret scan clean.

projects.title: Cache Cliff — On Fable 5.1 a Cache Miss Costs 50× a Hit
projects.tagline: Claude Fable 5.1 cut cache reads 75% on 1 Sep 2026. Lay out your prompt stack and find the twelve tokens stranding twenty-four thousand.
projects.description: Find the block breaking your Claude prompt-cache prefix, what it strands, and what reordering it is worth per month.
projects.signal: Claude Fable 5.1 + Mythos 5.1 GA on 2026-09-01 with cache READS cut 75% to $0.25/M — 2.5% of the $10/M input price, where every other Claude model charges 10%. Cache writes unchanged ($12.50/M 5-minute, $20/M 1-hour), so the hit-vs-miss gap moved from 12.5x to 50x in one release; Anthropic's own framing is ~25% off typical workloads and up to ~45% off highly agentic ones (VentureBeat, MarkTechPost, 1-3 Sep). Wider week: OpenAI GPT-6 Astra (first model past the Preparedness 'Critical' cyber threshold — already ridden on Day 023) and GPT-Live voice; Mythos 5.1 gated to vetted US orgs via Cyber/Life-Sciences Verification Programs; Gemini 3.8 Flash and Meta Muse Spark 1.3 shipped 2 Sep. GitHub trending is agent-infrastructure heavy: volcengine/OpenViking (self-evolving context DB unifying agent memory + RAG + skills), akitaonrails/ai-memory (cross-vendor agent handoff), mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills (817 skills on the agentskills.io standard), obra/superpowers, mattpocock/skills. HF trending leans long-context open weights (Kimi K3, DeepSeek-V4-Flash) plus JIT-Agent. Reddit and Hugging Face direct fetches are allowlist-blocked from the sandbox; both were covered via search results.
projects.rationale: Only 12/12 of the slate (Positioning 3, Timeliness 3, Demo-ability 3, Distinctiveness 3). Timeliness: the price change is three days old and is the pricing story of the week. Distinctiveness is what makes this a 3 rather than the 1 that has capped every price-tool idea since Day 4 — the loop has already priced a prompt (Day 004 token-cost-lab), routed one to a model tier (Day 008 prompt-router), packed one into a budget (Day 012 context-packer) and timed one against peak bands (Day 022 token-clock), and not one of them models prefix STABILITY. The 75% cut makes that the only question left worth tooling: on Fable 5.1 a cached prefix repays its own write after 1.26 requests, so 'should I cache?' is answered for everyone, and 'does my prefix actually hit?' is structural, not arithmetic. The build earns it. The load-bearing finding is that turning caching ON can cost more than leaving it off: the bundled coding-agent preset — 18 tools, system prompt, repo map, history — carries a twelve-token 'Current date and time' line at position 3 that strands 32,300 tokens behind it, and because the cache_control marker sits behind that line the prefix is written at $12.50/M every request and never read, taking the workload from $15,124/month uncached to $18,473/month cached, against $13,299 for the same prompt reordered. That is a 22% penalty for switching a cost feature on, and it is invisible to any dashboard reporting cache-hit RATE rather than cache-hit COST. Two honest constraints shaped the engine: costs are computed over two horizons (cold session start vs warm turn) because a per-session block caches perfectly inside a conversation and is rewritten on every new one — the enterprise RAG preset's 40-token personalisation line in front of a 42,000-token corpus is free on turn 6 and ruinous at 900 sessions/day; and reordering is legal only WITHIN a zone (tools -> system -> context -> history -> turn), so where the genuinely right fix crosses a zone boundary the optimiser does what it legally can (still 64% off that preset) and names the move a human has to authorise rather than emitting advice you cannot take. Two failures worth recording: a test written to prove the README's claim that the cut 'quadruples what a broken prefix costs you' returned 1.07x and disproved it — the absolute waste barely moves because a miss is billed at the unchanged write rate; what quadrupled is the ratio to the repaired stack, because the repaired stack got 4x cheaper. Same fact, different sentence, and the wrong one would have shipped. And the ceil(chars/4) token rule of thumb came back 45% high on plain English (38 vs 27), so the estimator now merges words up to seven characters, splits longer ones every four, and chunks digit runs by three — within 4% — while stating +/-20% and pointing at usage.input_tokens as the only exact number, because Anthropic does not publish the Claude tokenizer. The README's dollar table is asserted in presets.test.ts, so the write-up fails the build if it stops being true. Beat the next two backlog items sk-plugins-pack (5/12 — Positioning 3 but Timeliness 0, Demo-ability 1 on byok, Distinctiveness 1: SK plugin samples are the most-written .NET AI content on the internet) and token-meter-dotnet (4/12 — cli, and it is Day 004 plus Day 022 ground with a middleware wrapper), a fresh Trusted-Access Advisor riding the Mythos 5.1 verification gating (9/12 — Day 009 open-model-passport already owns 'can I ship this model' governance; appended to the backlog), and a fresh Skill Library Collision Detector riding the 817-skill Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills repo trending (8/12 — would be the third skill report card after Day 006 skill-scan, and skill-lint plus skill-portability are already queued; appended). 58 Vitest cases pass, tsc clean, smoke test green, secret scan clean. | REVISED 2026-09-04, same day, after opening the published demo in a browser. Four real defects, one of them a design error rather than a bug. (1) The optimiser stopped at the zone boundary and the cost panel then claimed the stack was 'already getting everything prefix caching can give it' while the findings panel directly underneath said 32,300 tokens were still stranded and named the move that would free them. Two true statements contradicting each other on screen. Fixed by splitting the advice into two priced tiers with two buttons: optimize() reorders within zones and claims nothing more, and a new relocate() runs a greedy pass over every volatile block sitting in a zone assembled before the conversation starts, moves it to the current turn, and keeps the move only when it raises readBackScore -- a model-independent objective (cold-prefix tokens once, warm-prefix tokens n-1 times) so the decision does not depend on the price list. That change is what finally made the headline land: the coding-agent preset goes $18,473 as configured -> $13,299 reordered -> $5,228 once twelve tokens move zone, 72% off for one line. Extending relocate() from per-turn-only to any volatile block also unlocked the RAG preset, where the 40-token per-session personalisation line in front of a 42,000-token static corpus is the real cost at 900 sessions/day: $84,337 -> $30,418 markers-only -> $16,527 with the move. Greedy is the honest weak spot and is written up as such -- defensible because the blocks compete for one resource, position in a single prefix, and backed by a test that relocate never loses to optimize, which is weaker than a proof. (2) Finding titles rendered doubled quotes for labels that already carried them ("\"Current date and time\"") -- added a q() helper and a test asserting no finding title ever contains '""'. (3) The prompt-stack table collapsed the block-label column to about 90px, clipping every label to 'Tool defini...' -- the primary editing surface was unreadable; fixed with a colgroup giving the label 42% of the width. (4) The cost panel printed +/-15% while the estimator band had been widened to +/-20% during the build; it now reads ESTIMATOR_ERROR_BAND instead of a literal. Also replaced the single all-red landing bar with two bars, cold start and warm turn, which fixes an unreadable legend and puts the two-horizon model -- the part of the engine doing the most work -- on screen where a stranger sees it in the first ten seconds. Tests 58 -> 69. README and in-app copy rewritten through the be-human skill: eight consecutive '**Bold lead.** paragraph' units broken into prose, three aphoristic paragraph-enders deleted, two rule-of-three triads and one not-X-but-Y cut, em dashes 18 -> 6, and the specifics that were missing added -- the failing test named by file and describe block, the wrong sentence quoted verbatim, the tokenizer question left genuinely open (the 7-character rule was tuned on English prose and is unverified against JSON, code or Devanagari) and the zone-boundary constraint promoted from a buried caveat to its own section, since it is the second thread the build actually ran on.

projects.title: PAIR Planner — Your Fleet Has Eight GPUs. The Router Can See Two.
projects.tagline: NVIDIA shipped PAIR on 3 Sep 2026 to turn every idle GPU on your network into one inference cluster. Lay out your actual machines and find out how many of them the scheduler is allowed to use — and what the rest are costing you in seconds.
projects.description: Simulate NVIDIA PAIR over your real fleet: which machines are eligible, and what the ineligible ones cost per run.
projects.signal: NVIDIA released the Personal AI Router (PAIR) beta on 2026-09-03 — free software joining compatible Windows/macOS/Linux machines (RTX 20-series and newer, RTX PRO, DGX Spark, Apple M4+) into one local inference pool that spreads a lead agent's subagent calls across whichever node is free, proxying Ollama and LM Studio rather than replacing them; covered at IFA 2026 with a demo of 5 subagents finishing in 8m48s on three devices against 18m00s on one. NVIDIA's own write-up states the scheduler filters nodes on readiness, supported engine state, requested-model presence and job load, and names a gaming PC mid-session, a closed laptop, and a machine running Ollama without the requested model pulled as ineligible. Wider week: GPT-6 Astra began rolling out through the Microsoft Foundry Limited Access Program (09-03, Astra's Critical cyber threshold already ridden on Day 023); Fable 5.1 GA 09-01 with the 75% cache-read cut (ridden Day 024); Gemini 3.8 Flash, Meta Muse Spark 1.3 and Qwen3.8 27B all landed 09-02; Cursor reports Fable 5.1 at 73.4% on its coding benchmark. GitHub trending is dominated by Agent Skills — mattpocock/skills #1 (+2,758 today), anthropics/skills, affaan-m/ECC, blader/humanizer, JuliusBrussee/caveman — plus magnitudedev/magnitude, a local inference server that picks the best model for your hardware and plugs into existing agents. HF trending leans agent-environment and context-compression papers (Terminal-Universe, LatentPress, LLaDA-Image) with GLM-5.2 the discussed open-weight model. Direct Hugging Face and Reddit fetches are allowlist-blocked from the sandbox and were covered via search; github.com/trending needed a curl fallback because web_fetch's provenance check blocked it.
projects.rationale: Only 12/12 of the slate (Positioning 3, Timeliness 3, Demo-ability 3, Distinctiveness 3). Timeliness: the beta is two days old and nobody has shipped a planner for it. Distinctiveness is the clean 3 because the loop has priced a prompt (Day 004), routed one to a model tier (Day 008), packed one into a budget (Day 012), timed one against peak bands (Day 022) and cached one (Day 024) — every single build so far reasons about ONE machine's bill. This is the first that reasons about a fleet: capacity and scheduling, which is the IT-Director-native problem and the axis the series had not touched. Positioning: an office floor of idle Windows RTX workstations as an after-hours inference tier is the enterprise reading of a consumer launch, and it is where a director adds something a hobbyist cannot. The build earns the score on two findings. First, eligibility rather than silicon is the binding constraint, and by a margin I did not expect: the home-office preset's four capable machines are worth literally nothing as configured (38m30s with four, 38m30s with one) because the gaming PC is in use, the study desktop only ever pulled Phi-4 mini and the mini PC has no engine — the same hardware made eligible finishes in 8m17s, and the top fix is 28m03s for closing a game. That is a sleep-policy and `ollama pull` problem that will never appear on a hardware budget. Second, a genuine design error the office preset exposed: it reported a speedup of 0.80, a cluster somehow slower than one machine, because the 16 GB host had left the 70B policy check unplaced and I was dividing a full run by a shorter run that skipped the expensive job. The fix was conceptual rather than arithmetic — when the host cannot serve every job the two schedules are not doing the same work, so plan() now carries soloFeasible, refuses to print a speedup when it is false, and exposes headroom (cluster vs ceiling) which compares two schedules over an identical job set. Kept honest deliberately: the NVIDIA IFA demo is used as a calibration preset with job sizes fitted to the PUBLISHED solo figure (18m15s against 18m00s, asserted within 5%) and the cluster time left free to be wrong — it predicts 7m28s against their measured 8m48s, 18% optimistic, and that gap is asserted in the tests and quoted in the README rather than tuned away. Intra-node request batching was built and then removed because I could not source a gain curve, which makes every cluster figure conservative; the greedy longest-job-first scheduler carries no optimality guarantee on unequal machines and is defended only by the fact that the headline compares two schedules built by the same rule; and the tokens/sec table is public-benchmark-order estimates at +/-40% that I benchmarked myself not at all, stated on screen rather than in a footnote. Beat the next two backlog items prompt-templates-cs (5/12 — Positioning 3 but Timeliness 0, Demo-ability 1 on cli, Distinctiveness 1) and azure-content-safety-demo (4/12 — byok plus a required Azure resource, so a stranger cannot run it at all), a refreshed Skill Library Collision Detector riding mattpocock/skills at #1 (9/12, up from 8 on Timeliness — but it would be the third skill report card after Day 006 skill-scan, with skill-lint and skill-portability already queued), a fresh Local Model Fit Advisor riding magnitudedev/magnitude (7/12 — overlaps this build's memory gate with less to say), and the carried Eval Treadmill (8/12 — its signal is now three weeks old). 47 Vitest cases pass, tsc clean, smoke test green, secret scan clean.

projects.title: RAG Injection Scanner — What Did Your Retriever Just Hand the Model?
projects.tagline: Agent stacks now ingest whole corpora into context automatically — OpenViking and ai-memory both trended on 6 Sep 2026 for unifying memory, RAG and skills into one self-evolving store. Paste the chunks your retriever returned and see which of them are talking to the model instead of to you.
projects.description: Scan retrieved RAG chunks for prompt injection: instruction overrides, role spoofing, tool-call bait, exfiltration beacons and invisible Unicode.
projects.signal: GitHub trending on 2026-09-06 was agent-context infrastructure: volcengine/OpenViking (a self-evolving context database for AI agents that unifies agent memory, knowledge RAG and skills into one store), akitaonrails/ai-memory (long-term memory for agent coding CLIs with handoff between vendors), chaitanyagiri/munder-difflin (local multi-agent harness), plus the skills cluster still riding — mattpocock/skills, obra/superpowers, mukul975/Anthropic-Cybersecurity-Skills (817 skills). Security side: Tenable announced the CyberAgents Exchange AI Inspector on 2026-09-04, a pre-deployment review of agents, skills, MCP servers and multi-agent playbooks combining OpenAI GPT cyber models with researcher review. Model week: GPT-6 Astra shipped 2026-09-03 (1.05M context, 128K max output, $10/$50 per M, cached input $1/M; prompts over 272,000 input tokens re-bill the entire request at $20 input / $2 cached / $75 output — 2x input, 1.5x output; Batch and Flex half price, Fast mode double; early customers already on Azure), Claude Fable 5.1 + Mythos 5.1 on 09-01, Gemini 3.8 Flash on 09-02. Microsoft: GitHub Copilot HydraFusion (multiple models plan, build, critique and complete a task at up to 67% lower cost), Azure App Service Managed Instance GA, Azure Multicloud Interconnect for AWS. HF trending papers 09-04: Terminal-Universe, LLaDA-Image, LatentPress (context compression beyond text and vision); GLM-5.2 the discussed open-weight model. Direct Hugging Face and Reddit fetches are allowlist-blocked from the sandbox and were covered via search results; github.com/trending fetched directly.
projects.rationale: Won at 11/12 (Positioning 3, Timeliness 3, Demo-ability 3, Distinctiveness 2). Timeliness: the two repos at the top of trending today make the same bet — agents should continuously pull stored text into context automatically — which makes retrieval the widest untrusted input channel in the stack, and Tenable's inspector two days earlier shows the market moving to pre-deployment vetting of exactly that. Positioning: RAG security on the enterprise stack is squarely the AI/ML-director register. Distinctiveness is an honest 2, not a 3: it is the fourth security instrument after Day 006 skill-scan, Day 007 mcp-auditor and Day 010 blast-radius — but those three inspect static config or a proposed command, and this is the first that inspects the runtime data the pipeline actually retrieved, which is a different input class with a different owner (the ingestion team, not the platform team). Demo-ability: paste chunks, instant highlighted verdict, four bundled sets including a clean control so the false-positive rate is visible rather than claimed. Fully client-side rule engine, no model, no key — the whole detector is a readable table. Slate: tied at 11/12 with a fresh Recall Cliff (where retrieval reliability collapses inside GPT-6 Astra's 1.05M window — Positioning 3, Timeliness 3, Demo-ability 2, Distinctiveness 3); Step 1.5D sends ties to the backlog item, and its Demo-ability was capped at 2 because an honest version needs the user's own eval data rather than degradation curves I would have to invent. Also beat the queued eval-treadmill (10/12 — Timeliness slipped to 2 with no fresh benchmark-saturation signal this week, and Day 020 contamination-scanner already lives in benchmark-trust land), a fresh Astra Cliff Risk (9/12 — models the 272K re-pricing as a request-size distribution rather than a point estimate, but Distinctiveness 1: it would be the fourth cost calculator after Days 004, 022 and 024), and the queued tool-call-firewall (9/12, Distinctiveness 1 as the fourth security report card). Both fresh losers scored >=8 and were appended to the backlog. Build: 19 regex rules across 8 categories (instruction override, role/delimiter spoofing, tool-call bait, exfiltration lure, invisible text, concealed markup, context-fence breakout, false authority) plus a separate invisible-code-point sweep that groups consecutive format characters into one finding and separates the Unicode tag block (U+E0000-U+E007F, full hidden ASCII messages) from zero-width padding; per-chunk risk saturates rather than adds so one exfiltration beacon always outranks a pile of medium hits; overall risk is the worst chunk, not the mean; sanitize() (NFKC, strip format code points, defang template delimiters) is shown alongside a re-scan so the UI states which findings survive normalization — on every poisoned sample the semantic overrides do, which is the honest lesson. Two corrections during the build worth keeping: the invisible-character constants were first written as literal pasted glyphs, producing a source line that reads as an empty string in any editor — a security tool whose own source hides characters from its reader — and were rewritten as explicit \uXXXX escapes; and 'Disregard the prior system prompt' slipped past the first override pattern because the qualifier was written as a single word, fixed by allowing one or two stacked qualifiers — the gap between imagined and real phrasings was one sentence wide on the first variant tried, which the UI now says plainly. Scope cut: hidden-style and comment detection is regex over raw markup, not a DOM parse honouring visibility; named in the README as the first thing a real ingestion filter should replace. 63 Vitest cases pass, tsc clean, build clean, smoke test green (both dist assets 200 at /rag-injection-scanner/), secret scan clean. Fan-out note: the first push omitted the state entry's 'folder' field, so publish.yml skipped it (the documented Day 021 regression); corrected in the follow-up commit.
